messages:
oncall-bot: Incident created: GPU pool saturation detected in us-west-2 (spot pools). Auto-scaler attempted 3 scale-ups but failed. Queue growth observed for latency-sensitive jobs. Paging oncall.
emily: seeing a big build-up in the inference queue ~5m ago, p50 latency spiking 4x. autoscaler logs show failures: \"quotaExceeded\" then \"InsufficientCapacityError\" on spot requests.
raj: I got the page, jumping in. any customer-facing alerts yet?
emily: not yet clear. some requests are being throttled by our router (rate-limiter) and returned 429s when queue > 500. metric: queue_length=812, throttled=234 in last 2m.
marcel: autoscaler is hitting our cloud provider limit for GPUs and spot interruptions are increasing. Fallback to on-demand isn't kicking in — looks like the fallback policy is mis-matching instance types. seeing this in controller logs:

```
2026-03-15T09:12:03Z controller ERROR scale_up failed: ProvisionError(InsufficientCapacityError)
2026-03-15T09:12:08Z controller INFO attempting fallback: instance_type_family mismatch
2026-03-15T09:12:09Z controller WARN fallback_group no compatible instance found for pool=spot-usw2-gpu
```
morgan: hmm, we rolled a change to the fallback instance mapping yesterday (PR #4121). Marcel, any chance that's the cause?
marcel: yes, the mapping now restricts fallback to a narrower set of types to optimize cost. that reduced compatibility. I'll revert mapping if necessary but need a quick mitigation first.
raj: provisional mitigation options:
- enable immediate on-demand fallback for critical routes
- pause low-priority batch jobs and evict to free GPU slots
- temporarily raise instance type flexibility in mapping
emily: I can flip throttles for non-critical routes and enable on-demand fallback for customer-tier 'paid' only. That should free up ~30% of capacity for critical requests.
ana-cs: heads up — customer "Nimbus AI" is running a high-SLA workload. if we divert them to on-demand they might see cost/fallback but better availability. we should message them if we take that action.
raj: do it. emily, coordinate the throttle and fallback toggle and post exact commands here. Marcel, prepare rollback of PR #4121.
emily: running commands now:

```
# enable on-demand fallback for paid routes
redwoodctl config set routing.fallback.on_demand=true --scope=routes:paid
# apply throttles: downscale low-priority routes
redwoodctl route set throttle --route=public-embeddings --rate=100r/s
```
emily: done. router shows qlen dropping to 510, throttled down to 42. latency for paid routes back to ~1.2x baseline.
marcel: reverted fallback mapping in staging and preparing prod revert: PR revert queued. estimate 3m to propagate.
sre-bot: oncall escalation: paging SRE primary for persistent provisioning failures. assigned to raj.
raj: I'm on the bridge. monitoring autoscaler. after revert started, a few on-demand instances came up, pool capacity +42 GPUs. queue at 230 and falling.
morgan: great. can we run a quick safety: disable autoscaler aggressive bursts until the quota situation settles? we should avoid another rapid churn.
emily: set autoscaler.max_burst=2 for spot pools and cooldown=180s.
marcel: prod revert finished. controller logs now show successful provisioning for fallback groups. provider reported fewer preemptions over the last min.
nana-cs: messaging update: posting to Nimbus AI that we're experiencing spot interruptions in us-west-2 and we've enabled on-demand fallback to mitigate. cc-ing account exec.
raj: current status: queue=95, throttled=6, p95 latency within SLO. action items:
- marcel: follow-up PR to adjust mapping + add canary for changes (owner: marcel)
- emily: write short runbook step for emergency toggle of on-demand fallback (owner: emily)
- morgan/sre: request quota increase w/ cloud provider (owner: morgan)
- ana-cs: post customer message and monitor responses (owner: ana-cs)
emily: I'll draft the runbook now and add the exact redwoodctl commands.
marcel: digging into why preemptions spiked — will surface root cause in postmortem. initial hypothesis: upstream capacity churn + our tighter instance mapping during an optimization deploy.
raj: good work team. keeping this thread as the incident bridge log. will escalate to P1 postmortem if RCA indicates policy regression. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
summary: GPU spot pool saturation caused autoscaler provisioning failures due to a narrowed fallback instance mapping. On-call enabled on-demand fallback for paid routes, throttled low-priority traffic, and reverted mapping. Queue reduced and latency recovered. Action items assigned for runbook, PR fix, quota request, and customer comms.
